name: Jeff Darland

bio.statement: Darland's pamphlet statement lists Tigard Budget Committee service as his prior governmental experience.

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-37)

bio.statement: The pamphlet lists his occupational background as international engineering leadership and advanced manufacturing research and development.

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-37)

bio.statement: Darland says in his pamphlet statement that he left his career to care for his young children.
bio.excerpt: I stepped away from my career to care for my young children.

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-37)

positions.statement: Darland says his public service began with rate increases that led him to examine Tigard's water infrastructure, debt and capital plans.
positions.excerpt: Repeated rate increases prompted me to follow the numbers through Tigard’s water infrastructure, debt, and capital plans.

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-37)

positions.statement: In his pamphlet statement, Darland says he will push for plain-language explanations of utility rates, debt and major investments.
positions.excerpt: Clearer Government. I will push for plain-language explanations of utility rates, debt, and major investments.

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-37)

positions.statement: Darland's pamphlet statement supports thoughtful growth and partnerships using public land and community land trusts to create homes with lasting affordability.
positions.excerpt: I support thoughtful growth, and will pursue partnerships using public land and community land trusts to create homes with lasting affordability.

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-37)

positions.statement: Darland's pamphlet statement says new growth should pay its fair share and deliver lasting value such as walkable neighborhoods, safe streets and public spaces.
positions.excerpt: New growth should pay its fair share, and deliver lasting value: walkable neighborhoods, protected natural areas, safe streets, and public spaces that bring people together.

source.publisher: Washington County Voters' Pamphlet, Nov. 3, 2026 (page WC-37)
